names.significance: Her worship and Her mantra are to be kept hidden, revealed only by the guru; traditionally the name is also read from guhā 'cave', as She who dwells in the cave of the heart.

meaning_check.note: 'secret' stated first; the old phrase 'to be known in secret' is kept.

names.uncertain: Derived from √guh 'to hide' (gerundive) or from guhā 'cave' ('dwelling in the cave of the heart'); both are traditional.

samasa.vigraha: कैवल्यम् एव पदम् कैवल्यपदम्; कैवल्यपदस्य दायिनी कैवल्यपददायिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: kaivalyam eva padam kaivalyapadam; kaivalyapadasya dāyinī kaivalyapadadāyinī
samasa.explanation: (1) kaivalya-pada 'the state that is kaivalya' (karmadhāraya of identification). (2) dāyinī 'she who gives' is the head and takes that state in the genitive.

components.note: √dā 'to give' + the agent suffix -in (with y), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who bestows the state of kaivalya, final liberation
names.significance: Kaivalya is the Self standing alone, free of all that is not the Self; She grants it, being Herself kevalā (name 623).

meaning_check.note: pada 'state' and the term kaivalya rendered.

names.previous_split_issues: pada was glossed 'foot'; here it is 'state, station'.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (traditionally also read as tri + purā)
samasa.vigraha: त्रीणि पुराणि यस्याः सा त्रिपुरा; अथवा त्रिभ्यः पुरा त्रिपुरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: trīṇi purāṇi yasyāḥ sā tripurā; athavā tribhyaḥ purā tripurā
samasa.explanation: Grammatically a bahuvrīhi, 'She who has three cities (abodes)'; pura takes the feminine -ā. The traditional derivation reads the indeclinable purā 'before': 'She who was before the three (gods)'. Both are given by commentators.

components.meaning: city, abode (pura, with the feminine -ā); read also as the indeclinable purā 'before, of old'

names.meaning: She who is Tripurā, the Goddess of the three cities, prior to the three gods
names.significance: Every triad is in Her: the three worlds, the three bodies, the three states of waking, dream and sleep, the three powers and the three gods; Śrīvidyā names Her Tripurasundarī, the beauty of the three cities.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS put into IAST; the grammatical sense ('of the three cities') is added to the traditional 'older than the three'.

names.uncertain: Two derivations: tri + pura 'three cities' (bahuvrīhi) and tri + purā 'before the three' (the traditional reading). The meaning gives both.

sandhi.rule: jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

samasa.vigraha: त्रयाणाम् जगताम् समाहारः त्रिजगत्; त्रिजगता वन्द्या त्रिजगद्वन्द्या

samasa.explanation: (1) tri-jagat 'the three worlds' taken together (samāhāra-dvigu). (2) The gerundive vandyā 'to be saluted, praised' is the head and the three worlds are its agent, in the instrumental.

components.meaning: to be saluted, worthy of praise

names.meaning: She who is adored by the inhabitants of all three worlds
names.significance: Heaven, earth and the underworld all bow to Her.
names.previous_split_issues: jagad was given in its sandhi form; the stem is jagat (d by jaśtva before v).

samasa.explanation: A bahuvrīhi with a numeral first member: 'She who has three forms'. The feminine numeral tisraḥ appears as the stem tri- in the compound; mūrti is already feminine.

names.meaning: She who has three forms (as Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva)
names.significance: Creating, sustaining and dissolving, She takes the three forms of the gods (or of their powers Brāhmī, Vaiṣṇavī and Raudrī), being Herself the One behind them.

meaning_check.note: 'the aggregate of the trinity' replaced by the bahuvrīhi 'having three forms'; ITRANS names put into IAST.

samasa.explanation: īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head and tridaśa 'the gods' stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the gods'. tridaśa is a fixed word for the gods.

components.note: lit. 'the thirty' (three times ten), a round number for the thirty-three gods; traditionally also explained as those always in the third state of life (youth)

names.meaning: She who is the ruler of the gods
names.significance: Indra and all the gods hold their sovereignty from Her, as name 607 also says.
names.previous_split_issues: The old split gave tri 'three' + daśeśvarī 'ruler of the thirty'; the members are tridaśa 'the gods' + īśvarī, joined by guṇa.

samasa.explanation: A collective numeral compound, 'the group of three syllables'; a dvigu ending in -a takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.21 dvigoḥ). She is identified with that three-syllable whole.

components.note: akṣara, with the -ī of the dvigu

names.meaning: She who is the three-syllabled (mantra)
names.significance: Traditionally the three syllables are read as a, u and m of Oṃ, as the three seed-syllables of the Bālā mantra (aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ, compare name 622), or as the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī (name 588).

meaning_check.note: The explanation 'Oṃ = a u m' is one of several and is moved to the significance.

names.uncertain: Which three syllables are meant is explained in more than one way (Oṃ, the Bālā mantra, the three kūṭas).

samasa.vigraha_iast: divyaḥ gandhaḥ divyagandhaḥ; divyagandhena āḍhyā divyagandhāḍhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) divya-gandha 'divine fragrance' (karmadhāraya). (2) āḍhyā 'rich, abounding' is the head and takes the fragrance in the instrumental: 'rich in divine fragrance'.

names.meaning: She who is richly endowed with divine fragrance
names.significance: Her body is naturally fragrant; traditionally the scent of the flowers and unguents offered to Her comes from Her, not to Her (compare name 13).
names.previous_split_issues: gandhāḍhyā was left as one row; it is gandha 'fragrance' + āḍhyā 'rich in'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha_iast: sindūrasya tilakam sindūratilakam; sindūratilakena añcitā sindūratilakāñcitā
samasa.explanation: (1) sindūra-tilaka 'a tilaka of vermilion' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa of material). (2) The participle añcitā 'adorned' is the head and takes the tilaka in the instrumental.

components.meaning: tilaka, the auspicious mark on the forehead

names.meaning: She who is adorned with a tilaka of vermilion
names.significance: The vermilion mark is the sign of the auspicious married woman: it marks Her eternal union with Kāmeśvara.

meaning_check.note: Two overlapping glosses merged; the typos 'witha' and 'vermillion' removed.

names.previous_split_issues: tilakāñcitā was left as one row; it is tilaka 'forehead-mark' + añcitā 'adorned'.

names.meaning: She who is Umā (Pārvatī)
names.significance: Kālidāsa (Kumārasambhava 1.26) derives the name from her mother's cry u mā, 'O, do not!', forbidding her austerities; in the Kena Upaniṣad Umā Haimavatī appears to Indra and teaches him Brahman.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'pArvatI devI' put into IAST and the name Umā given.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: शैलानाम् इन्द्रः शैलेन्द्रः; शैलेन्द्रस्य तनया शैलेन्द्रतनया
samasa.vigraha_iast: śailānām indraḥ śailendraḥ; śailendrasya tanayā śailendratanayā
samasa.explanation: (1) śaila-indra 'the lord of mountains', Himavat (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; indra at the end of a compound means 'chief, king'). (2) tanayā 'daughter' is the head.

components.meaning: lord, chief (at the end of a compound)

names.meaning: She who is the daughter of Himavat, the king of the mountains
names.significance: Born again as Pārvatī after giving up Her body as Satī (name 598), She won Śiva by Her austerities.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'himavat' put into IAST and capitalized.

names.meaning: She who has a fair complexion
names.significance: In a Purāṇic story Pārvatī, teased for Her dark skin, performed austerities and became golden-fair, Gaurī; Gaurī is also the name given to the girl worshipped as the Goddess.

samasa.explanation: The participle sevitā 'served' is the head; the Gandharvas are its agent, in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She who is served by the Gandharvas (such as Viśvāvasu)
names.significance: The celestial musicians serve Her with song; Viśvāvasu, their chief, is traditionally named among them.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'gandharvas', 'vishvAvasu' put into IAST.

samasa.explanation: A bahuvrīhi, 'She in whose womb is the universe'; garbha takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: garbha, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who contains the whole universe in Her womb
names.significance: The universe is held within Her before it is born and after it is withdrawn.

samasa.explanation: A bahuvrīhi, 'She whose womb holds gold' (or 'whose womb is golden'); garbha takes the feminine -ā. The name echoes Hiraṇyagarbha, 'the golden embryo', the first-born source of the world.

components.note: garbha, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose womb is golden, the source of the world (as Hiraṇyagarbha)
names.significance: Hiraṇyagarbha, the golden embryo of Ṛgveda 10.121, is the first manifest form from which the world unfolds; She is that golden source.

meaning_check.note: The old meaning ('the cause of the universe') stated only an interpretation; the name says Her womb is golden, recalling Hiraṇyagarbha.

names.uncertain: The old meaning gave an interpretation ('the cause of the universe'); the literal bahuvrīhi and its echo of Hiraṇyagarbha are given here. Bhāskararāya's own gloss of this name was not confirmed.

samasa.explanation: -da 'cutting down' is from √do 'to cut' with the suffix ka (Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ) and the feminine -ā; avara 'the low, the base' is its object: 'She who cuts down the base (the demons)'.

components.meaning: low, base, inferior; here the demons

names.meaning: She who destroys the base (the demons)
names.significance: She cuts down whatever is low and opposed to the good, outward demons and the base tendencies of the mind.

meaning_check.note: 'the unholy' made exact: avara is 'the low, the base' (traditionally the asuras).

names.uncertain: The derivation from √do 'to cut' is the traditional one; -dā could also be read from √dā 'to give' ('She who gives even to the lowly'). The name is avaradā, not varadā: the avagraha in the verse marks the elided a.

samasa.explanation: adhīśvarī 'presiding sovereign' is the head and vāc 'speech' stands to it in the genitive: 'the presiding sovereign of speech'.

names.significance: All speech, from the Veda to ordinary words, arises from Her (compare name 577); She is Sarasvatī and more than Sarasvatī.

samasa.explanation: The gerundive gamyā 'to be reached' is the head; dhyāna 'meditation' is the means, in the instrumental.

names.significance: She is reached not by argument but by steady meditation; the next names say why She cannot be reached otherwise.

samasa.explanation: The negative na (a- before a consonant) is compounded with the gerundive paricchedyā 'to be delimited': 'not to be delimited'.

names.significance: She is not bounded by space, time or any object; compare name 701, deśakālāparicchinnā.

samasa.explanation: -da 'giving' is from √dā with the suffix ka (Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ), feminine -ā, with jñāna as its object.

names.meaning: She who bestows knowledge
names.significance: Traditionally the knowledge meant is knowledge of the Self, which frees.

samasa.explanation: A bahuvrīhi, 'She whose body is knowledge'; vigraha takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She whose very body is knowledge
names.significance: Her form is not made of matter: it is knowledge itself taking shape.

components.meaning: Vedānta, the Upaniṣads (lit. 'the end of the Veda')

names.meaning: She who is to be known through all the Upaniṣads
names.significance: All the Upaniṣads converge on one meaning (Brahma Sūtra 1.1.4, tat tu samanvayāt), and that meaning is She.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner dvandva)
samasa.vigraha: सत्यम् च आनन्दः च सत्यानन्दौ; स्वम् रूपम् स्वरूपम्; सत्यानन्दौ स्वरूपम् सत्यानन्दस्वरूपम्; सत्यानन्दस्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति सत्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: satyam ca ānandaḥ ca satyānandau; svam rūpam svarūpam; satyānandau svarūpam satyānandasvarūpam; satyānandasvarūpam asyāḥ asti iti satyānandasvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) satya-ānanda 'truth (being) and bliss' (dvandva; a karmadhāraya 'true bliss' is also possible). (2) sva-rūpa 'own form, essential nature'. (3) The two are identified (karmadhāraya), and the possessive -in with feminine -ī gives 'She whose essential nature is truth and bliss'.

names.meaning: She whose very nature is truth (being) and bliss
names.significance: Sat and ānanda, with cit, are the classic description of Brahman (compare name 700, saccidānandarūpiṇī); She is that being and bliss itself.

meaning_check.note: svarūpa is 'essential nature' rather than 'form'; satya rendered 'truth (being)'.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'lopAmudrA', 'agastya' put into IAST.

samasa.vigraha: लीलया कॢप्तम् लीलाकॢप्तम्; ब्रह्माण्डानाम् मण्डलम् ब्रह्माण्डमण्डलम्; लीलाकॢप्तम् ब्रह्माण्डमण्डलम् यस्याः सा लीलाकॢप्तब्रह्माण्डमण्डला
samasa.vigraha_iast: līlayā kḷptam līlākḷptam; brahmāṇḍānām maṇḍalam brahmāṇḍamaṇḍalam; līlākḷptam brahmāṇḍamaṇḍalam yasyāḥ sā līlākḷptabrahmāṇḍamaṇḍalā
samasa.explanation: (1) līlā-kḷpta 'fashioned in play' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa: līlā is the manner, in the instrumental). names.meaning: She who has fashioned the whole sphere of the universe in play
names.significance: Creation costs Her no effort and serves no need: it is līlā, play (compare Brahma Sūtra 2.1.33, lokavat tu līlākaivalyam).

samasa.explanation: The negative na (a- before a consonant) is compounded with the gerundive dṛśyā 'to be seen': 'not to be seen'.

names.meaning: She who is invisible, beyond the reach of the senses
names.significance: The Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad (1.1.6) calls the Imperishable 'that which cannot be seen, cannot be grasped'; She is not an object of the senses.

names.significance: Since nothing exists apart from Her, there is no object standing over against Her; She is the seer without a seen.

names.meaning: She who is the knower
names.significance: The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (2.4.14) asks: 'By what should one know the knower?' She is that knower, never the known.

samasa.explanation: The participle varjitā 'devoid of' is the head and vedya 'the knowable' stands to it in the instrumental: 'free from anything to be known'.

names.meaning: She who has nothing to be known apart from Herself

components.meaning: she who possesses yoga; a yoginī

names.significance: She is ever in union (yoga) with Śiva; the yoginīs who attend Her in the Śrīcakra and in the bodily centers are Her own powers.

names.meaning: She who bestows the power of yoga
names.significance: Success in yoga, and the union that is its goal, come by Her grace.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner itaretara-dvandva of three karmadhārayas)
samasa.vigraha: इच्छा एव शक्तिः इच्छाशक्तिः; ज्ञानम् एव शक्तिः ज्ञानशक्तिः; क्रिया एव शक्तिः क्रियाशक्तिः; इच्छाशक्तिः च ज्ञानशक्तिः च क्रियाशक्तिः च इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तयः; इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तयः स्वरूपम् इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तिस्वरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तिस्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: icchā eva śaktiḥ icchāśaktiḥ; jñānam eva śaktiḥ jñānaśaktiḥ; kriyā eva śaktiḥ kriyāśaktiḥ; icchāśaktiḥ ca jñānaśaktiḥ ca kriyāśaktiḥ ca icchāśaktijñānaśaktikriyāśaktayaḥ; icchāśaktijñānaśaktikriyāśaktayaḥ svarūpam icchāśaktijñānaśaktikriyāśaktisvarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti icchāśaktijñānaśaktikriyāśaktisvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) Three karmadhārayas of identification: icchā-śakti 'the power that is will', jñāna-śakti 'the power that is knowledge', kriyā-śakti 'the power that is action'. (2) The three form a dvandva. (3) They are identified with sva-rūpa 'own nature', and the possessive -in with feminine -ī gives 'She whose own nature is the powers of will, knowledge and action'. The members meet without sound change.

names.meaning: She who is in the form of the powers of will, knowledge and action
names.significance: Will, knowledge and action are the three powers of the one consciousness, by which every act of creation proceeds: first the will, then the knowing of what is willed, then the doing. Traditionally they are placed at the three corners of the central triangle of the Śrīcakra.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.explanation: ādhārā 'support' is the head and sarva 'all' stands to it in the genitive: 'the support of all'. ādhāra takes the feminine -ā because it describes Her.

names.meaning: She who is the support of all
names.significance: Everything rests in Her as the pot rests on the ground, while She rests on nothing else.

sandhi.rule: after a prefix ending in i, the s of sthā becomes ṣ (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and th then becomes ṭh by retroflex assimilation (8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ)

samasa.vigraha_iast: suṣṭhu pratiṣṭhā yasyāḥ sā supratiṣṭhā; athavā śobhanā pratiṣṭhā supratiṣṭhā
samasa.explanation: As a bahuvrīhi, su 'well, firmly' qualifies pratiṣṭhā 'standing, foundation': 'She whose standing is firm'. As a prādi-tatpuruṣa: 'the excellent foundation' (of the world). pratiṣṭhā is already feminine.

names.meaning: She who is firmly established
names.significance: She stands on Herself and on nothing else, and is the firm ground on which all else stands (name 659).
names.previous_split_issues: pratiṣṭhā was misspelt pratīṣṭhā (long ī; corrected); su was glossed 'beautiful', here it is 'well, firmly'.

sandhi.rule: jaśtva: the final t of sat becomes d at the end of a member, here before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte); the t of asat is voiced in the next junction

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvandva and karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: सत् च असत् च सदसती; सदसती एव रूपे सदसद्रूपे; सदसद्रूपयोः धारिणी सदसद्रूपधारिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sat ca asat ca sadasatī; sadasatī eva rūpe sadasadrūpe; sadasadrūpayoḥ dhāriṇī sadasadrūpadhāriṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) sad-asat 'being and non-being' (dvandva). (2) They are identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya): 'the forms that are being and non-being'. (3) dhāriṇī 'she who bears, assumes' is an agent noun and the head, with the forms as its object in the genitive.

components.note: causative of √dhṛ 'to hold', agent suffix -in, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who assumes the forms of both being and non-being
names.significance: In the Gītā (9.19) the Lord says 'I am being and non-being'; She holds both the manifest and the unmanifest, the real and the apparent.
names.previous_split_issues: sad and asad were given in their sandhi forms; the stems are sat and asat (t → d by jaśtva).

verse_notes.note: Names 601–602 return to Her eyes and smile, both qualified by dara 'gently'. Name 606 ends in the ū-stem bhū, so its nominative is -bhūḥ.
Name 609 refers to the dahara-vidyā of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (8.1.1); name 610 fills the whole second half and names the lunar days from pratipad to the full moon.
Name 614 fills the second half; its two pairs correspond in order: Ramā (Lakṣmī) on the left, Vāṇī (Sarasvatī) on the right.

verse_notes.note: Both avagrahas mark a name beginning with a-: name 639 is avaradā (not varadā), name 642 is aparicchedyā. Name 640: vāg is the c of vāc voiced before adhīśvarī.
Name 648 is spelled with vocalic ḷ: कॢप्त (kḷpta), as in name 21.
Names 649–652 pair off: unseen and without anything seen, the knower and without anything to know. Names 653–657 play on yoga (yoginī, yogadā, yogyā, yogānandā) and close with yugandharā.
Name 658 fills the whole first half: the three powers of will, knowledge and action.

report.summary: Checked all 61 names of ślokas 121–130 against text.json: sandhi at every member junction and visible prefix junction (including ud + jval, pari + cheda, sam + vedya, the augment m in yugandharā), a layered samāsa with pausa-form vigrahas, and each meaning against that analysis. Two meanings were replaced (638 stated only an interpretation; 651 added an object the name lacks) and 40 were tidied (ITRANS to IAST, typos, words not in the name such as 'daily' in 610 and 'maintained' in 648). Several old splits misdivided members (629 tridaśa + īśvarī, not tri + daśeśvarī; 657 yuga + the augment m) or gave sandhi forms as stems (jagad, vāg, sad/asad, pratipan). No problem was found in the Sanskrit; external sandhi joins names in ślokas 121, 124, 125 and 127, where the avagrahas mark avaradā (639) and aparicchedyā (642).
